title: Snapdragon Guardian API Guide
content: The Snapdragon Guardian API is broken into two sections: The Main API and the Device Management (DM) API. The Main API is used to send commands to the device and view their responses. Most API are asynchronous (as the device may be offline when the API is called) while others return cached responses from the device. The Device Management (DM) API is used to store cached data about each device. All API calls are synchronous, as they do not go to the device. Authentication: All endpoints require authentication headers (see Deployment Package for token setup).
heading: Overview

The Device Management (DM) API is used to store cached data about each device. All API calls are synchronous, as they do not go to the device.
All endpoints require authentication headers (see Deployment Package for token setup).

title: Snapdragon Guardian API Guide
content: List Devices → GET {DM}/v1/devices Get details of a device → GET {DM}/v1/devices/{deviceId} Send a command to the device → POST {Main}/devices/{deviceId}/command Get the status of a command → GET {Main}/devices/{deviceId}/command/{sequence} Get command history → GET {Main}/devices/{deviceId}/commands Get event history → GET {Main}/events Get details of an event → GET {Main}/events/{eventId} Full details of all API are available in the swagger Main API: https://base-url/qrms/swagger/index.html Device Management: https://base-url/dm/swagger-ui/index.html

heading: 5. Get command history

children.value: Get a recent history of all commands run on the device. This can be helpful if sequence number is lost, or to get the most recent result for a given command request type.
By default, Snapdragon Guardian will only retain the most recent 100 commands. This can be configured by updating the MAX_COMMANDS_PER_DEVICE in the infrastructure package.
